findings.title: App API dispatcher still reads the appStore barrel synchronously, breaking all app OAuth callbacks and app webhooks
findings.body: This PR changes every value of the default export of `@calcom/app-store` from the app's module namespace to a Promise of that namespace. The catch-all API route `apps/web/pages/api/integrations/[...args].ts`, which dispatches every app's API endpoints (`/api/integrations/{app}/add`, `/callback`, `/webhook`, etc. — e.g. the Google Calendar OAuth callback and the Stripe payment webhooks) looks the app up synchronously as `const app = appStore[appName as keyof typeof appStore]` and then checks `"api" in app` before calling `app.api[endpoint](req, res)`. It is not among the updated files, so after this change `app` is a Promise, the `in` check is false, and the route falls through to its error/404 path for every app. Consequence: connecting/disconnecting any integration and all payment webhooks stop working. The lookup must become `const app = await appStore[appName as keyof typeof appStore]`. It is also worth grepping the whole repo for any other remaining `appStore[...]` / `getCalendar(` consumers, since the barrel's contract changed from synchronous module to Promise and only the call sites in this PR were migrated.

findings.title: The dynamic imports still execute eagerly — importing the barrel immediately loads all 28 app chunks
findings.body: Each registry entry is written as `applecalendar: import("./applecalendar")`, so every `import()` expression is invoked at the moment `packages/app-store/index.ts` is evaluated. Only the *awaiting* became lazy, not the *loading*: the first import of `@calcom/app-store` still triggers fetching and evaluating all 28 app modules, so the startup/module-load cost this PR is presumably trying to reduce is essentially unchanged (only code-splitting/parallel async evaluation is gained). If the intent is to load an app only when it is actually used, the values need to be thunks (`() => import("./applecalendar")`) or a lazy getter/Proxy, with call sites adjusted accordingly. A side effect of creating all 28 promises up front is that a chunk-load failure in an app that is never used still produces an unhandled promise rejection (most entries are never awaited), which crashes Node under the default unhandled-rejections behavior.
